method: Regression guard, not a benchmark claim. Generous peak-RSS ceilings per fresh child process and a post-GC heap-growth ceiling for one long-lived MCP server, measured by scripts/memory-bench.mjs. Ceilings sit well above the recorded values so runner noise cannot fail them, and well below the pre-fix behavior they guard against.

runner.measurement: peak RSS from process.resourceUsage().maxRSS inside each child (preload probe); MCP heap is process.memoryUsage().heapUsed after two forced GCs, sampled after the warm-up calls and after the last call

check.rationale: ark-check --json --no-cache over the fixture. 450 MiB ceiling.

doctor.rationale: ark-check --doctor --json --no-cache over the fixture: the scan, the compact importer index doctor keeps for files nothing imports (ADR 0037), and every advisory section. 500 MiB ceiling; recorded 196 MB at n=2000 (macOS arm64, Node 26).

hookWrite.rationale: One-line Write through the PreToolUse hook. It must not walk or parse the tree: 200 MiB ceiling (loading TypeScript is most of the floor).

hookPatch.rationale: Complete ApplyPatch (atomic base/candidate preflight over the tree). 500 MiB ceiling.

mcp.rationale: One long-lived MCP server over repeated validate_code / ark_prepare_write / ark_prepare_change / ark_check calls. Post-GC heap may not grow more than 16 MiB between the end of warm-up and the last call (a leak or an unbounded cache exceeds that); 700 MiB peak RSS ceiling.
